source.title: Algebraic integers with conjugates in a prescribed distribution
source.version: arXiv:2111.12660v2, posted 16 March 2024, 47 pages, dated 19 March 2024 inside the file, with the arXiv comment '47 pages'; v1 is from 24 November 2021. items.name: Totally positive algebraic integers, the trace ratio and the constant λ_SSS
items.statement: For an algebraic integer α with conjugates α₁ = α, α₂, …, α_n, the degree is deg(α) = n and the trace is tr(α) = α₁ + ⋯ + α_n; α is totally positive if all its conjugates are positive reals. Define λ_SSS to be the greatest real number (equivalently, the supremum of the real numbers λ with this property) such that for every ε > 0 there are only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers α with tr(α) < (λ_SSS − ε)deg(α).
items.note: Corrected using E1: the finite-exception property is downward closed, so there is no least such real number. Equivalently λ_SSS is the least limit point of the trace-to-degree ratios. Historical bounds: Schur e^{1/2}, Siegel 1.7336, Smyth 1.7719, Wang–Wu–Wu 1.793145; the upper bound before Smith was 2. The classical constant and auxiliary method extend CA.6; their absence is not a claim that all CA.6 arithmetic is missing.

items.name: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem
items.statement: Fix ε > 0. Show that there are only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers α with tr(α) ≤ (2 − ε)deg(α), and explicitly compute the exceptions if possible. This is Borwein's codification of the problem, and reflects the general consensus that λ_SSS should equal 2.
items.note: The paper's Theorem 1.1 shows the consensus is wrong: λ_SSS < 1.89831. Not planned by any layer.

items.name: Smyth's auxiliary-polynomial method and the resultant argument
items.statement: Suppose for a given λ > 0 one has positive reals a₁, …, a_N and nonzero integer polynomials Q₁, …, Q_N with x ≥ λ + Σ_k a_k log|Q_k(x)| for all x > 0. Summing over the conjugates of a totally positive algebraic integer α whose minimal polynomial P is coprime to every Q_k, and using that ∏_{i≤n} Q_k(α_i) = res(P, Q_k) is a nonzero integer, gives tr(α) ≥ λ deg(α).
items.note: Smyth's original article realises this with λ = 1.7719 and about fifteen auxiliary polynomials; the state of the art uses 130 polynomials and λ = 1.793145. Smyth and Serre observed that there are λ < 2 for which no such inequality can hold; this was usually read as a limitation of the method, and the paper vindicates Smyth's opposite reading. Not planned; the integrality of the resultant is the only obstruction that survives (Theorem 1.5).

items.name: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant is less than 1.89831
items.statement: λ_SSS < 1.89831. In particular there are infinitely many totally positive algebraic integers α with tr(α) < 1.89831 · deg(α), so the expected value λ_SSS = 2 is wrong.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Theorem 1.1, p. 2; proved in Example 5.16, pp. 42–43
items.note: The constant is not optimal for two reasons recorded in Remark 1.2: the paper uses rounded forms of the optimal parameters for Serre's example, and even optimised Serre's argument cannot produce the true value of λ_SSS (Proposition 5.17). The proof applies the main theorem to an explicit measure built from Serre's two-part integration argument.

items.name: Extreme point counts for simple abelian varieties over finite fields
items.statement: There is C > 0 such that for every square prime power q ≥ C there are infinitely many F_q-simple abelian varieties A over F_q with #A(F_q) ≥ (q + 2√q − 0.89831)^{dim A} and infinitely many more with #A(F_q) ≤ (q − 2√q + 2.89831)^{dim A}.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Corollary 1.3, p. 3; deduced from Theorem 1.1 by Proposition 5.13
items.note: Smith’s application imports general Honda–Tate from the shared AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli Part II route and Weil weights from DWP.1/R34.2. It belongs with the potential-theoretic optimization (route 1), not in the foundational Honda–Tate development. Further optimization and nonsquare q are not claimed by Corollary 1.3.

items.name: Counting measures of polynomials and the weak* topology
items.statement: For α ∈ ℂ let δ_α be the Dirac measure. For a complex polynomial P(z) = a_n ∏_{i≤n}(z − α_i) of degree n ≥ 1, the counting measure is µ_P = (1/n)(δ_{α₁} + ⋯ + δ_{α_n}), a probability measure on the roots. For Σ ⊂ ℂ compact, the Borel measures supported in Σ carry the weak* topology: µ_k → µ if and only if ∫f dµ_k → ∫f dµ for every continuous f : Σ → ℝ. Throughout, 'measure' means a finite positive Borel measure on ℂ.
items.note: Fresh statement read at the pins: TauCeti/Probability/Process/EmpiricalMeasure.lean:48–66 takes any nonempty Fintype, hence Fin n for n≥1, with the roots indexed with multiplicity. The normalized Dirac sum is exactly µ_P; no new counting-measure definition is needed. Mathlib FiniteMeasure.lean:726 and ProbabilityMeasure.lean:364 characterize convergence by bounded continuous real test functions; on compact Σ every continuous function is bounded. Definition 1.4 includes all finite positive measures, so the finite-measure carrier is retained, not just ProbabilityMeasure. Neither ST.0 nor OptimalTransport is a missing supplier.

items.name: The main theorem: which measures are limits of conjugate distributions
items.statement: Let Σ be a compact subset of ℝ with at most countably many connected components and capacity strictly greater than 1, and let µ be a Borel probability measure with support in Σ. Then the following are equivalent: (1) ∫_Σ log|Q(x)| dµ(x) ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q; (2) there is an infinite sequence of distinct irreducible monic integer polynomials R₁, R₂, … with supp(µ_{R_k}) ⊆ Σ for every k and µ_{R_k} → µ in the weak* topology.
items.note: The implication (2) ⇒ (1) is Serre's, and follows from the upper semicontinuity of log|Q| together with log|res(R_k, Q)| ≥ 0. The converse is the new content and occupies most of the paper: the only obstruction to realising a measure as a limit of conjugate distributions is the integrality of resultants, which is exactly Smyth's method. The restriction to countably many components is probably necessary — there are totally disconnected compact subsets of ℝ of capacity greater than 1 containing no algebraic number — while the restriction to Σ ⊂ ℝ and to capacity > 1 is expected to be removable, the capacity-1 case reducing by Proposition 5.7 to the unweighted equilibrium measure and being known only in special cases.

items.name: Logarithmic potential, energy, capacity and the equilibrium measure
items.statement: For Σ ⊂ ℂ compact and µ a Borel measure on Σ, the potential function is U^µ(z) = ∫_Σ −log|z − w| dµ(w) and the energy is I(µ) = ∫_Σ U^µ dµ ∈ ℝ ∪ {∞}. The capacity of Σ is κ_Σ = sup_µ e^{−I(µ)} over probability measures supported in Σ. If κ_Σ > 0 the supremum is attained by a unique probability measure of minimal energy, the unweighted equilibrium measure µ_Σ of Σ.
items.note: The foundational notions of logarithmic potential theory, equivalently the transfinite diameter and Chebyshev constant of a compact set. They appear nowhere in the atlas: a search of every stage description for 'capacity', 'equilibrium measure', 'logarithmic potential' and 'transfinite diameter' returns nothing, and the single hit for 'potential theory' is the Tau Ceti PDE roadmap's lane on maximum principles and harmonic functions, which is a different subject.

items.name: Hölder measures
items.statement: A Borel measure µ on ℝ is η-Hölder for η > 0 if there is C > 0 with µ([x, y]) ≤ C(y − x)^η for all x < y; µ is Hölder if it is η-Hölder for some η > 0.
items.note: The regularity class in which almost all of the paper works. It is exactly what makes the potential function continuous (Lemma 2.3) and the layer-cake identity (2.2) effective.

items.name: Potentials of Hölder measures are Hölder continuous
items.statement: For η ∈ (0,1) and µ an η-Hölder measure supported in a compact subset of ℝ, the potential U^µ is a finite, η-Hölder continuous function on ℝ: there is C > 0 with |U^µ(y) − U^µ(x)| ≤ C|y − x|^η for all x, y.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.3, p. 6, using the layer-cake identity (2.2) and Tonelli's theorem
items.note: The identity ∫_I log|x − t| dµ(t) = log b · µ(I) − ∫₀^b r^{-1} µ([x−r, x+r] ∩ I) dr for I ⊆ [x−b, x+b] is where the Hölder condition enters, and it recurs throughout §§2–4.

items.name: Compact finite unions of intervals
items.statement: A compact Σ ⊂ ℝ is a compact finite union of intervals if it is nonempty, has finitely many connected components and has no isolated points.
items.note: The class of sets to which the hard part of the proof is reduced by Proposition 2.5.

items.name: Reduction to Hölder measures on compact finite unions of intervals
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact with at most countably many components and capacity > 1, and let µ be a probability measure on Σ satisfying condition (1) of Theorem 1.5. Then there are Hölder probability measures µ₁, µ₂, … and closed subsets Σ₁, Σ₂, … of Σ such that each Σ_k is a compact finite union of intervals containing supp(µ_k), each µ_k satisfies ∫_{Σ_k} log|Q| dµ_k ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q, and µ_k → µ weak*.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Proposition 2.5, p. 7; proved in §5
items.note: The reduction that makes the rest of the argument possible; its proof uses the convolution and sweetening constructions of §5. Use one-point components, not isolated points, and finite energy I(µ)<∞; see E6–E7 and items 64–66.

items.name: The weight w_µ and the n-norm
items.statement: For a Hölder measure µ supported in a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, the weight is w_µ(z) = exp(U^µ(z)) ∈ ℝ_{>0} ∪ {∞}. For a complex polynomial P and n ≥ 0, the n-norm of P with respect to (µ, Σ) is ‖w_µ^n P‖_Σ = max_{x ∈ Σ} (w_µ(x)^n |P(x)|).
items.note: The weighted supremum norm of weighted potential theory. Everything in §§3–4 is an estimate for such norms; the target is to produce integer polynomials whose n-norm grows subexponentially.

items.name: A criterion for weak* convergence of counting measures
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact and µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ. Let P₁, P₂, … be real monic polynomials of increasing degree with all roots in Σ, and suppose ‖w_µ^{deg P_n} P_n‖_Σ^{1/deg P_n} → 1. Then µ_{P₁}, µ_{P₂}, … converge to µ in the weak* topology on Σ.
items.note: The bridge from the norm estimates to the statement of Theorem 1.5: it is the last step of the proof in §4.1. Imported weighted inputs are separated in items 57–60, with exact Saff–Totik locators.

items.name: Removing a root changes the n-norm by a polynomial factor
items.statement: Let Σ be a compact finite union of intervals and µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ. There is C > 0 depending on Σ and µ such that for all n ≥ 0, m ≥ 1, every complex polynomial P of degree m and every root α of P, the polynomial Q(z) = P(z)/(z − α) satisfies ‖w_µ^n Q‖_Σ ≤ (2·max(n,m))^C ‖w_µ^n P‖_Σ.
items.note: A workhorse estimate used in §3 to pass between a polynomial and its cofactors, and in the proof of Lemma 3.8. The missing Remez supplier is item 67.

items.name: The gcd of integer polynomials and primitivity
items.statement: For nonzero integer polynomials Q₁, …, Q_k, gcd(Q₁,…,Q_k) is the unique integer polynomial G of maximal degree with positive leading term, primitive coefficients, and dividing each Q_i in ℚ[z]; by Gauss's lemma each Q_i/G is an integer polynomial.
items.note: Gauss's lemma and primitive polynomials are in Mathlib (`Polynomial.IsPrimitive`, `Polynomial.IsPrimitive.Int.dvd_iff_map_cast_dvd_map_cast` and the `IsIntegrallyClosed`/`UFD` content-and-primitive-part API), and CA.3 plans the surrounding integer-polynomial arithmetic. The particular normalisation used here is the paper's own bookkeeping.

items.name: A squarefree integral combination of integer polynomials
items.statement: Let k ≥ 1, n ≥ 0 and let Q₁, …, Q_k be nonzero integer polynomials of degree at most n with some Q_i of degree exactly n, and put G = gcd(Q₁,…,Q_k). Then there are nonnegative integers b₂, …, b_k, each at most 2(n − deg G), such that (Q₁ + b₂Q₂ + ⋯ + b_kQ_k)/G is squarefree of degree n − deg G.
items.note: A purely polynomial-arithmetic statement: a generic small integral combination of polynomials with a common factor removed is squarefree. It is used in the proof of Theorem 3.1 to produce the squarefree integer polynomial the geometry of numbers then adjusts. CA.3 plans integer-polynomial arithmetic with resultants and discriminants, and is the natural owner, but does not state this. Discriminant and finite-grid nonvanishing are library items 72 and 69; no new multivariate interpolation project is required.

items.name: The approximating polynomial of a measure
items.statement: For Σ ⊂ ℝ compact, µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ and n ≥ 1, let α_i be the least α ∈ Σ with µ((−∞, α]) = i/n for 0 ≤ i ≤ n, and set P_{n,µ}(z) = ∏_{i=1}^n (z − α_i). Then −n^{-1} ≤ (µ_{P_{n,µ}} − µ)((−∞, x]) ≤ 0 for all x, so |(µ_{P_{n,µ}} − µ)(I)| ≤ n^{-1} for every closed interval I.
items.note: The quantile discretisation of µ, whose roots are the nodes at which all later interpolation and evaluation arguments take place.

items.name: Discriminant and weight estimates for the approximating polynomial
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact and µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ. There is C > 0 determined by Σ and µ so that for all n ≥ 2, with α₁, …, α_n and P_{n,µ} as above, n^{−Cn} exp(−½n²I(µ)) ≤ ∏_{1≤i<j≤n} |α_i − α_j|, and, setting ρ_{n,µ}(x) = min_i |x − α_i|, one has n^{−C}ρ_{n,µ}(x) ≤ w_µ(x)^n |P_{n,µ}(x)| ≤ n^C ρ_{n,µ}(x) for all x ∈ Σ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Proposition 2.12, p. 10, equations (2.7) and (2.8)
items.note: The quantitative link between the energy of µ and the Vandermonde determinant of the discretisation; it is what converts potential-theoretic information into the determinant bound that the geometry of numbers consumes. E2 corrects the proof after (2.14) in Proposition 2.12: the exponential is |P_{n,µ}|.

items.name: Existence of squarefree integer polynomials of small weighted norm
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact and µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ with ∫ log|Q| dµ ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q. Then there is C > 0 determined by µ and Σ such that for every n ≥ 2 there is a squarefree integer polynomial R_n of degree n with ‖w_µ^n R_n‖_Σ ≤ n^{C√n}.
items.note: The first main output of the geometry-of-numbers section, proved from Proposition 3.6, Lemma 3.8 and Lemma 2.10 by an extremal argument over the gcd degrees m_k. It supplies the squarefree modulus for the coefficient adjustment of Corollary 3.3.

items.name: A flatness-theorem estimate for integer polynomials
items.statement: There is C > 0 such that: given positive integers c, n and a squarefree integer polynomial Q(z) = c(z − α₁)⋯(z − α_n) with the α_i distinct, writing Q_i(z) = Q(z)/(z − α_i), every real polynomial P of degree at most n − 1 admits complex numbers β₁, …, β_n with Σ_i |β_i| ≤ Cn log 2n such that P(z) − Σ_i β_i Q_i(z) is an integer polynomial.
items.note: An application of the flatness theorem of the geometry of numbers: the lattice of integer polynomials is not far from any real polynomial in the basis dual to evaluation at the roots of Q. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1 plans the Blichfeldt and Minkowski convex-body and successive-minima theorems, but a search of every stage description for 'flatness theorem', 'covering radius' and 'successive minima' outside GN.1's own title finds nothing, and this statement is not planned. Item 68 records BLPS Corollary 2.5, not Minkowski II, as the flatness supplier.

items.name: Approximating a real polynomial by an integer polynomial in the weighted norm
items.statement: Let Σ be a compact finite union of intervals and µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ. For n > 1, a real polynomial P of degree at most n − 1 and a squarefree integer polynomial Q of degree n, there is an integer polynomial R of degree at most n − 1 with ‖w_µ^n(P − R)‖_Σ ≤ n^C ‖w_µ^n Q‖_Σ, where C > 0 depends only on Σ and µ.
items.note: The coefficient-adjustment step in its final form: Theorem 3.2 makes P congruent to an integer polynomial modulo the lattice spanned by the Q_i, and Lemma 2.8 bounds the resulting error by the norm of Q.

items.name: A product bound for successive minima of evaluation polytopes
items.statement: Let m ≥ 0, let α₁, …, α_{m+1} be distinct reals and v₁, …, v_{m+1} positive reals, and let K be the set of real polynomials P of degree at most m with v_i|P(α_i)| ≤ 1 for all i. For 0 ≤ i ≤ m let λ_i be the least nonnegative real with λ_iK containing i + 1 linearly independent integer polynomials. Then D/(m+1)! ≤ λ₀λ₁⋯λ_m ≤ D, where D = ∏_i v_i · ∏_{i<j} |α_i − α_j|.
items.note: Minkowski's second theorem applied to the convex body cut out by weighted evaluation conditions, with the Vandermonde determinant computing the covolume. It is the engine of §3 and, like Theorem 3.2, belongs to the geometry-of-numbers layer GN.1 rather than to potential theory. E3 corrects the scalar domain: K is symmetric, so arbitrary negative dilation factors cannot define a minimum.

items.name: A lower bound for products of weighted norms
items.statement: Let µ be a Hölder probability measure on a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, let n, m ≥ 0, let R be a nonzero integer polynomial and let Q₀, …, Q_m be linearly independent integer polynomials of degree at most m. If ∫_Σ log|R| dµ ≥ 0, then ∏_{i=0}^m ‖w_µ^n Q_iR‖_Σ ≥ (1/(m+1)!) exp((mn − ½m² + n − ½m)I(µ)).
items.note: The lower half of the extremal estimate, obtained from Proposition 3.4 with v_k = |(R·Q_k)(α_k)|^{-1}.

items.name: Near-sharpness of the product bound
items.statement: Let Σ be a compact finite union of intervals, µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ and n ≥ 2. Then there are linearly independent integer polynomials Q₀, …, Q_n of degree at most n with ∏_{i=0}^n ‖w_µ^n Q_i‖_Σ ≤ n^{Cn} exp(½n²I(µ)), where C > 0 depends only on µ and Σ.
items.note: The matching upper bound, proved by applying Proposition 3.4 to the nodes of the approximating polynomial with v_k = |P_k(α_k)|^{-1} and using Proposition 2.12 and Lemma 2.8 to control the resulting norms. E10 restores the bound for every k≤n+1 before (3.5).

items.name: Nonpositivity of the energy of an admissible Hölder measure
items.statement: Let µ be a Hölder probability measure on a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ with ∫_Σ log|Q| dµ ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q. Then I(µ) ≤ 0.
items.note: The paper describes this as the statement that accounts for the discriminant of a squarefree integer polynomial being a nonzero integer. It is generalised to arbitrary Borel measures in Proposition 5.7, which is what the reduction of Proposition 2.5 needs.

items.name: The gcd-refined lower bound for products of weighted norms
items.statement: Let µ be a Hölder probability measure on a compact finite union of intervals Σ. There is C > 0 such that for 0 ≤ k ≤ m ≤ n with n ≥ 2 and linearly independent integer polynomials Q₀, …, Q_m of degree at most n with ‖w_µ^n Q₀‖_Σ ≤ ⋯ ≤ ‖w_µ^n Q_m‖_Σ, setting G = gcd(Q₀,…,Q_k) and assuming ∫_Σ log|G| dµ ≥ 0 and m = max_{i≤k} deg(Q_i/G), one has ∏_{i=0}^m ‖w_µ^n Q_i‖_Σ ≥ n^{−Cn} exp((mn − ½m²)I(µ)).
items.note: Combines Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.5: the auxiliary polynomials H_j built from Theorem 3.2 applied to ½z^j are linearly independent because their images in F₂[z] are, which supplies the missing directions in the lattice.

items.name: The key construction: real polynomials with many integral coefficients
items.statement: Let Σ be a compact finite union of intervals of capacity κ > 1, µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ and B > 0. There is C > 3 depending on Σ, µ, B such that for every integer n > C, setting m = ⌊B√n log n⌋, there is a real monic polynomial P_n of degree n which (1) is squarefree with all roots in Σ, (2) satisfies ‖w_µ^{n−m}P_n‖_Σ ≤ n^Cκ^m, (3) has even integer coefficients in every degree k ∈ [n−m, n−1], and (4) has roots α₁ < ⋯ < α_n admitting x₁ < α₁ < y₁ < ⋯ < x_n < α_n < y_n with [x_k, y_k] ⊆ Σ and min(w_µ(x_k)^{n−m}|P_n(x_k)|, w_µ(y_k)^{n−m}|P_n(y_k)|) ≥ n^{−C}κ^m.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Proposition 4.1, p. 21, equations (4.1) and (4.2)
items.note: The technical heart of the paper. Given it, Theorem 1.5 follows in §4.1: split P_n into its top m + 1 coefficients, which are already even integers, and a real tail; use Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.3 to replace the tail by 4R(z) − 2 for an integer polynomial R; the resulting monic integer polynomial R_n is within the margin (4.2) of P_n at every x_k and y_k, so it has one root in each [x_k, y_k] and no others, it is irreducible by Eisenstein at 2, and ‖w_µ^n R_n‖_Σ^{1/n} → 1, so Lemma 2.7 applies.

items.name: Chebyshev polynomials of a compact set
items.statement: For r ≥ 0 there is a unique real monic polynomial T_r of degree r for which there are r + 1 points x₀ < ⋯ < x_r in Σ with (−1)^{r−i}T_r(x_i) = ‖T_r‖_Σ for all i; it satisfies C^{-1}κ^r ≤ ‖T_r‖_Σ ≤ Cκ^r with C > 1 depending only on Σ, where κ is the capacity.
items.note: The classical equioscillation characterisation of Chebyshev polynomials of a compact set, together with the identification of the limit of ‖T_r‖_Σ^{1/r} with the capacity. The atlas has Chebyshev polynomials only as an orthogonal basis of L²([−1,1]) in the Tau Ceti completed roadmap on orthogonal bases, which is a different object and does not give these bounds.

items.name: Pruned polynomials
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and P a real monic squarefree polynomial with root set S, suppose there is a subset S̃ ⊆ S ∩ Σ of cardinality n such that for every connected component I of Σ meeting S, the set I ∩ S̃ contains neither the least nor the greatest element of I ∩ S. Then ∏_{α ∈ S̃}(z − α) is a degree n pruned polynomial of P.
items.note: The device for discarding the roots nearest the ends of each component of Σ, where the equioscillation control degrades.

items.name: A modified Chebyshev polynomial with a controlled sign pattern
items.statement: There is C > 0 depending only on Σ such that for every r ≥ 2 there are a real monic polynomial T̃_r of degree r with ‖T̃_r‖_Σ ≤ r^Cκ^r, an integer k₁ ≤ k₀, and reals y₁ < ⋯ < y_{r+k₁} in Σ with |T̃_r(y_i)| ≥ C^{-1}κ^r for all i, such that (y₁, y_{r+k₁}) contains all the roots of T̃_r and each (y_i, y_{i+1}) either does not lie in Σ and contains no root of T̃_r, or lies in Σ and contains exactly one root.
items.note: Here k₀ is the number of connected components of Σ; the proof compares T̃_r with T_{r+3k₀}. This is the polynomial along which the coefficient adjustment is performed. E8 replaces the proof’s quotient-root assertion by roots in the convex hull of Σ; the fixed-degree quotient bound still holds.

items.name: The coefficient-adjustment lemma of Robinson and Fekete–Szegő
items.statement: Let P be a monic real polynomial of degree n and r ≥ 2, with y₁ < ⋯ < y_{r+k₁} constructed from T̃_r as in Lemma 4.4. Then there is a monic real polynomial T of degree r such that the degree i coefficient of T^D P is an even integer for every i ∈ [(D−1)r + n, Dr + n − 1], and T(y_i)/T̃_r(y_i) ≥ 1/2 for all i, with ‖T‖_Σ ≤ r^{C₁}κ^r + 2C₁rκ^r.
items.note: The technique goes back to Robinson and to Fekete and Szegő, Theorem D: one adjusts the top coefficients of a power of an auxiliary polynomial to be integral while keeping its size under control. Here D = ⌈4C₁²/(κ−1)⌉ is fixed once Lemmas 4.2 and 4.4 hold with C = C₁. The signed inequality preserves the sign of T̃_r at every y_i; an absolute-value bound would not justify the r sign changes in Lemma 4.7.

items.name: Complementary polynomials
items.statement: Given Σ, κ, C₁, D as above, a real monic P of degree n and r ≥ 2, take T from Lemma 4.5 and set Q₀(x) = ∏_{j=0}^{D−1}(T(x) − ((2j+1)/(4DC₁))κ^r). With d = rD − r, choose ε_d, …, ε₁ ≥ 0 minimal in turn so that (Q₀ + ε_dT_d + ⋯ + ε_iT_i)·P has an even coefficient in degree d + n + 1 − (d − i + 1), and put Q = Q₀ + ε_dT_d + ⋯ + ε₁T₁ + N with N ≥ 0 minimal so that |Q(α)| ≥ n^{-1}C₂^{-1}κ^{Dr} at every root α of P, where C₂ = 8(4DC₁)^D. This Q is the complementary polynomial to P of degree Dr, and every coefficient of PQ in the relevant range is an even integer.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Definition 4.6, pp. 25–26, equations (4.7) and (4.8)
items.note: The construction that produces, from an arbitrary monic real polynomial, a partner making the product have a long block of even integer coefficients while keeping all roots in Σ.

items.name: Complementary polynomials are squarefree with well-separated roots in Σ
items.statement: There is C > 1 such that for r ≥ C, n ≥ 0 and P real monic of degree n with complementary polynomial Q of degree Dr: Q is squarefree with all roots in Σ, and every root β of Q lies in an interval [x, y] ⊆ Σ containing no other root of Q with |Q(x)|, |Q(y)| ≥ C^{-1}κ^{Dr} (Lemma 4.7). Moreover ‖Q‖_Σ ≤ r^Cκ^{Dr} and ‖Q′‖_Σ ≤ r^Cκ^{Dr}, and for every root β, |Q(x)| ≥ C^{-1}κ^{Dr}|x − β| for x ∈ [β − r^{-C}, β + r^{-C}] (Lemma 4.8).
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemmas 4.7 and 4.8, pp. 26–28, equation (4.11)
items.note: The two estimates that make condition (4) of Proposition 4.1 available for the complementary factor. E9 includes all 0≤j<D intervals; E11 uses a union-of-forbidden-shift-intervals argument for N≤na.

items.name: Well-separated approximating polynomials
items.statement: With Σ and µ fixed and d an integer, there is C > 0 such that for every n ≥ 2 there is a monic squarefree polynomial P̃_n of degree n with: every root α having [α − n^{-C}, α + n^{-C}] ⊆ Σ and containing no other root; w_µ^{n+d}(x)|P̃_n(x)| ≥ n^{-C} min_α|x − α| for all x ∈ Σ; and ‖w_µ^{n+d}P̃_n‖_Σ ≤ n^C.
items.note: A pruned and perturbed form of the approximating polynomial of Definition 2.11, and the other factor of P_n = P̃_{n−Dr}Q_{Dr} in the proof of Proposition 4.1.

items.name: The measure ν_[a,b] and its potential
items.statement: For b > a > 0 let ν_{[a,b]} be the measure on [a,b] with dν_{[a,b]}(t) = √(ab) dt/(πt√((b−t)(t−a))). It is a 1/2-Hölder probability measure, for every z ∈ ℂ, U^{ν_{[a,b]}}(z) + log|z| − log((a + 2√(ab) + b)/(b−a)) vanishes for z ∈ [a,b] and is ≤ 0 otherwise, and U^{ν_{[a,b]}}(0) = log((a + 2√(ab) + b)/(4ab)).
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Notation 5.1 and Lemma 5.2, pp. 31–32, equation (5.1)
items.note: The pushforward under z ↦ 1/z of the equilibrium measure of [b^{-1}, a^{-1}], and the second of the two measures in Serre's argument; it is also the smoothing kernel used in Notation 5.3. At z = 0 the inequality is interpreted in the extended reals. Smith cites balayage [24, (II.4.47)] for mass one, but his own substitution u = 1/t reduces the mass integral to that of the reciprocal-interval arcsine measure. Thus no separate general balayage construction is required by this extraction; general balayage at the end of p.45 is a suggested future method.

items.name: Smoothing by convolution and its effect on potentials
items.statement: For ε ∈ (0,1/2), put ν_ε = ν_[ε²,ε]. For a finite positive Borel measure µ supported in compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, µ*ν_ε is 1/2-Hölder, supported in {x : [x−ε,x−ε²] meets Σ}. For every z ∈ ℂ, U^{µ*ν_ε}(z) ≤ U^µ(z) + µ(Σ) log((ε²+2ε^{3/2}+ε)/(ε−ε²)) ≤ U^µ(z) + µ(Σ) C√ε, with an absolute C; use the corresponding difference inequality wherever U^µ(z) is finite. If the convolutions are supported in Σ for all sufficiently small ε, they converge weak* to µ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Notation 5.3 and Lemma 5.4, p. 33, equation (5.5)
items.note: Corrected E4 retains the arbitrary finite mass allowed in Notation 5.3 and avoids an undefined infinity subtraction. For µ=Mδ₀ and z ∈ [ε²,ε], the potential difference is exactly M times the displayed logarithm; M>1 disproves the printed mass-independent bound. Subsequent uses have mass at most one. Tietze extension is item 71, supplied by Mathlib.

items.name: Sweetened measures
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact of capacity κ > 1, Σ′ ⊇ Σ compact, µ a probability measure and ν a measure on Σ′ with γ = 1 − ν(Σ′) ∈ [0,1]. Let µ_Σ be the unweighted equilibrium measure of Σ and B = sup_{U^µ(z)<∞}(U^{ν+γµ_Σ}(z) − U^µ(z)), assumed finite; then B ≥ 0. The sweetened measure of ν with respect to Σ and µ is sw(ν) = (β + γ − βγ)µ_Σ + (1−β)ν, where β ∈ [0,1) satisfies β/(1−β) = B/log κ; β + γ − βγ is the measure of sweetener. It satisfies U^{sw(ν)}(z) ≤ (1−β)U^µ(z) for all z.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Definition 5.5, pp. 34–35, equations (5.7) and (5.8)
items.note: The device that restores the admissibility condition after smoothing, by adding a controlled amount of equilibrium measure. Remark 5.6 records that for Σ = [x₁,y₁] ∪ ⋯ ∪ [x_k,y_k] the equilibrium measure has density |P(t)|∏_i|t−x_i|^{-1/2}|t−y_i|^{-1/2} for a polynomial P, so it is 1/2-Hölder and sweetening preserves the Hölder condition.

items.name: Nonpositivity of the energy in general
items.statement: Let µ be a Borel probability measure with support in a compact subset of ℝ such that ∫ log|Q| dµ ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q. Then I(µ) ≤ 0.
items.note: The removal of the Hölder hypothesis from Corollary 3.7, proved by smoothing and sweetening inside a long interval. It is what shows that at capacity exactly 1 the only candidate measure is the unweighted equilibrium measure. The weak lower semicontinuity of energy is item 63.

items.name: The optimisation constants λ(Σ, F) and λ_Smyth(Σ, F)
items.statement: Let Σ ⊆ ℝ be closed with at most countably many components and capacity > 1, and F : Σ → ℝ continuous with F(x_i)/log|x_i| → +∞ along any sequence with |x_i| → ∞ when Σ is unbounded. Enumerating the algebraic integers α_i all of whose conjugates lie in Σ, with degrees n_i and minimal polynomials P_i, set λ(Σ,F) = liminf_i ∫_Σ F dµ_{P_i}. Let λ_Smyth(Σ,F) be the least upper bound of the λ for which there are nonzero integer polynomials Q₁,…,Q_N and positive a₁,…,a_N with F(x) ≥ λ + Σ_i a_i log|Q_i(x)| for all x ∈ Σ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Notation 5.8 and Theorem 5.11, pp. 37 and 39, equations (5.11) and (5.15)
items.note: Example 5.9 records that F(x) = x and Σ = ℝ_{≥0} give λ(Σ,F) = λ_SSS, so the trace problem is the model case of this class of optimisation problems.

items.name: Reduction of the optimisation to a compact subset
items.statement: Given Σ and F as above, there is a compact Σ₀ ⊆ Σ such that for every probability measure µ with compact support in Σ but not in Σ₀ there is a probability measure µ′ supported in Σ₀ with ∫F dµ > ∫F dµ′ and with ∫log|Q| dµ′ ≥ 0 for every integer polynomial Q with ∫log|Q| dµ ≥ 0.
items.note: The step that handles unbounded Σ, using the growth condition (5.11) on F.

items.name: Smyth's method computes the optimum
items.statement: For Σ and F as in Notation 5.8, λ(Σ, F) = λ_Smyth(Σ, F).
items.note: The vindication of Smyth's method: the auxiliary-polynomial inequalities capture the true constant, so the apparent limitations of the method observed by Smyth and Serre are in fact limitations of the constant. Combined with Serre's example (Example 5.16), which shows no such inequality can hold for λ > 1.89830…, this proves Theorem 1.1. E5 records the zero-coefficient/root issue and the continuity/perturbation repair; separation and weak compactness are library inputs 70 and 51.

items.name: Point counts of abelian varieties over a finite field in terms of λ(Σ, F)
items.statement: Let q be a prime power, Σ = [−2√q, 2√q] and F(x) = log|q + 1 − x|. Then for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many F_q-simple abelian varieties A over F_q with #A(F_q)^{1/dim A} ≤ exp(λ(Σ,F) + ε), infinitely many more with #A(F_q)^{1/dim A} ≥ exp(−λ(Σ,−F) − ε), and only finitely many with #A(F_q)^{1/dim A} outside [exp(λ(Σ,F) − ε), exp(−λ(Σ,−F) + ε)].
items.note: Kadets [15], Proposition 2.1 (arXiv:1906.02264, p.3) gives the reduction. For a Weil q-number π use x=π+q/π=π+conj(π), a totally real algebraic integer with conjugates in [−2√q,2√q], and y=q+1−x. If P is the minimal polynomial of x, #A(F_q)^{1/dim A}=exp(∫log|q+1−t|dµ_P(t)); the Honda–Tate multiplicities cancel in this normalized identity. Equivalently #A(F_q)=∏_{i=1}^{dim A}(q+1−x_i) with conjugate-pair multiplicities. A real Weil number itself is ±√q. Remark 5.14 describes additional congruence freedom for ordinary, geometrically simple families, not a replacement for these hypotheses.

items.name: Explicit point-count bounds from the trace constant
items.statement: With λ_SSS as in Example 5.9 and any ε > 0, there is C > 0 such that for every square prime power q > C there are infinitely many F_q-simple abelian varieties with #A(F_q) ≥ (q + 2√q + 1 − λ_SSS − ε)^{dim A} and infinitely many more with #A(F_q) ≤ (q − 2√q + 1 + λ_SSS + ε)^{dim A}.
items.note: With Theorem 1.1 this gives Corollary 1.3. The link between the two optimisation problems is that near the endpoints of [−2√q, 2√q] the function log|q + 1 − x| is, after rescaling, the trace functional.

items.name: A sufficient criterion for admissibility via potentials
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact of capacity > 1 with at most countably many components and µ a probability measure on Σ. Suppose there are distinct irreducible primitive integer polynomials Q₁, …, Q_N and positive reals a₁, …, a_N with Σ_i a_i deg Q_i ≤ 1 and U^µ(z) ≤ −Σ_i a_i log|Q_i(z)| for all z ∈ ℂ, and suppose ∫_Σ log|Q_i| dµ ≥ 0 for each i. Then µ satisfies the equivalent conditions of Theorem 1.5.
items.note: The practical criterion by which a candidate measure is certified; it is how Example 5.16 verifies the hypotheses of Theorem 1.5 for Serre's measure.

items.name: Serre's measure and the proof of Theorem 1.1
items.statement: Take a = 0.087353, b = 4.411076, γ = 0.215485 and µ = γν_{[a,b]} + (1−γ)µ_{[a,b]}, where µ_{[a,b]} is the unweighted equilibrium measure of [a,b]. Then U^µ(z) + γ log|z| equals a constant C ≈ −1.3·10^{−7} on [a,b] and is at most C elsewhere, ∫log|x| dµ(x) ≈ 1.5·10^{−6} is nonnegative, so Proposition 5.15 applies with Q₁(z) = z; and ∫x dµ(x) = γ√(ab) + (1−γ)(a+b)/2 ∈ (1.898303, 1.898304). Applying Theorem 1.5 to µ proves Theorem 1.1.
items.note: The measure repackages, as a single convex combination, Serre's two-part argument in a letter to Smyth, which integrated the auxiliary inequality first against µ_{[a,b]} and then against the pushforward of the equilibrium measure of [b^{-1}, a^{-1}] under z ↦ 1/z — the latter being ν_{[a,b]}. The parameters a and b are rounded forms of the optimal ones.

items.name: Finitely many auxiliary polynomials never suffice
items.statement: Let Σ and F be as in Notation 5.8, let µ be a probability measure with compact support in Σ with ∫log|Q| dµ ≥ 0 for every nonzero integer polynomial Q and ∫F dµ = λ(Σ,F), and let P be an irreducible monic nonconstant integer polynomial with ∫_Σ F dµ_P < λ(Σ,F) whose roots lie in an open subset of ℝ contained in Σ. Then ∫_Σ log|P| dµ = 0 and the supports of µ_P and µ are disjoint.
items.note: The obstruction explaining Remark 1.2: an optimal measure must be orthogonal to every such P, so Serre's one-polynomial argument cannot produce λ_SSS, and the optimisation problems grow in complexity with the number of auxiliary polynomials. Uses the common domination input 61, rather than a separate potential-theory supplier.

items.name: Algebraic integers, conjugates, minimal polynomials and resultants
items.statement: For an integral element, its minimal polynomial and complex conjugates are defined. Over an integral domain, if f splits, Res(f,g) = lc(f)^{deg g}∏_{α root of f}g(α), with multiplicities. For monic integer P this gives Res(P,Q)=∏Q(α) ∈ ℤ, and it is nonzero when P,Q are coprime over ℚ.
items.note: AUDIT-18 CA.3 already marks resultants and discriminants built. Fresh read: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean:134,140,478,908. The product theorem assumes Splits over the working domain, so map integer polynomials to ℂ, use resultant_map_map, and specialize the leading coefficient to one. Nonvanishing is applied over ℚ/ℂ with the field hypothesis, not by pretending the field theorem applies directly to ℤ. minpoly is in FieldTheory/Minpoly/Basic.lean:41. The existing CA.3/upstream layers are consumers, not missing suppliers.

items.name: Eisenstein's criterion
items.statement: A monic integer polynomial whose non-leading coefficients are divisible by a prime p and whose constant term is not divisible by p² is irreducible over ℚ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), used in §4.1, p. 22, at the prime 2
items.note: The polynomials R_n constructed in §4.1 have the form z^n + ⋯ + 4R(z) − 2, so they are Eisenstein at 2; this is what makes them irreducible and hence minimal polynomials of algebraic integers. Mathlib has Eisenstein's criterion.

items.name: Tonelli's theorem and the monotone convergence theorem
items.statement: Tonelli's theorem for nonnegative measurable functions on a product of σ-finite measure spaces, and the monotone convergence theorem, used for the layer-cake identity (2.2) and for passing to the limit against the upper semicontinuous function log|Q|.
items.note: Both are in Mathlib's measure theory library, with the product-measure and Lebesgue-integral API.

items.name: Weak* compactness for probability measures on a compact set
items.statement: The set of Borel probability measures on a compact metric space is compact in the weak* topology, so every sequence has a convergent subsequence; used in the proof of Theorem 5.11 to extract a limit of the measures µ_N.
items.note: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Prokhorov.lean:175–179 supplies CompactSpace (ProbabilityMeasure E) for compact E; lines 183–185 also give the supported finite-measure version. LevyProkhorovMetric.lean:695 supplies metrizability on a separable Borel metric space. Apply these on compact Σ ⊂ ℂ and Topology/Sequences.lean:298 to obtain a convergent subsequence. All are present at the pin; no ST.0 or OptimalTransport planning dependency remains.

items.name: Minkowski's second theorem for successive minima
items.statement: For a discrete full lattice L in a d-dimensional real Euclidean space and a centrally symmetric convex body K with zero in its interior, (2^d/d!) covol(L) ≤ (∏_{i=0}^{d−1}λ_i(L,K)) vol(K) ≤ 2^d covol(L), where λ_i≥0 are the successive minima.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), §3, pp. 12–16, behind Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.4
items.note: The current GN.1 packet plans both bounds at GN.1/minkowski-second-lower and GN.1/minkowski-second-upper. AUDIT-02 distinguishes this missing theorem from the built Blichfeldt and first Minkowski theorems (items 73–74) and the built GN.0 lattice/covolume infrastructure. The evaluation-polytope specialization remains item 23 and flatness remains a separate missing input (68).

items.name: Honda–Tate theory
items.statement: The classification of isogeny classes of simple abelian varieties over a finite field F_q by conjugacy classes of Weil q-numbers, together with Tate's theorem computing Hom groups and endomorphism algebras through ℓ-adic Tate modules.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2, introductory application p.3 and Proposition 5.12 p.40, citing Honda [14]; Kadets [15], Proposition 2.1
items.note: General F_q Honda–Tate and rational Tate Hom are already routed by accepted PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/honda-tate and /tate-hom to the AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli Part II family. They are not yet actual atlas layers, so this item stays missing and route 4 merges the shared requirements under that parent. Faltings R28.4 is a completed number-field isogeny layer, not this finite-field classification. Retain arbitrary prime powers q here even where the Lipnowski–Tsimerman counting conclusions specialize to prime fields.

items.name: The Weil bound for abelian varieties over finite fields
items.statement: Frobenius eigenvalues π of an abelian variety over F_q are algebraic integers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value √q. A real eigenvalue equals ±√q. The totally real algebraic integer x=π+q/π=π+conj(π) has every conjugate in [−2√q,2√q]. Paired eigenvalues give #A(F_q)=∏_{i=1}^{dim A}(q+1−x_i), with multiplicities.
items.note: DWP.1 and R34.2 supply the abelian-variety Weil bound (R34.1 fixes weights). The interval in Proposition 5.12 is for π+q/π, not for a class called real Weil numbers. Item 43 records the normalized minimal-polynomial measure identity.

items.name: Upper semicontinuity of log|Q| and Serre's implication
items.statement: For a nonzero integer polynomial Q the function log|Q| is upper semicontinuous on a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, so for a weak*-convergent sequence of counting measures µ_{R_k} → µ one has ∫_Σ log|Q| dµ ≥ limsup_k ∫_Σ log|Q| dµ_{R_k} = limsup_k log|res(R_k,Q)|/deg R_k ≥ 0.
items.note: The easy implication (2) ⇒ (1) of Theorem 1.5, recorded here because it is the statement that identifies the resultant obstruction as the only one. It is elementary but has no owner in the atlas, and travels with the potential-theoretic items.

items.name: The equilibrium measure of a finite union of intervals
items.statement: If Σ = [x₁,y₁] ∪ ⋯ ∪ [x_k,y_k] with x₁ < y₁ < ⋯ < x_k < y_k, then the unweighted equilibrium measure has dµ_Σ(t) = |P(t)| dt ∏_{i≤k}|t − x_i|^{-1/2}|t − y_i|^{-1/2} on Σ for some polynomial P; in particular µ_Σ is 1/2-Hölder. For a single interval [a,b] this is the arcsine law dx/(π√((b−x)(x−a))).
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Remark 5.6, p. 35, and Example 5.16, p. 43
items.note: Retain missing: neither the equilibrium characterization nor the finite-union density follows from an orthogonality measure alone. The pinned Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT (Mathlib/.../Chebyshev/Orthogonality.lean:49) is the unnormalized arcsine density on (−1,1]; TauCeti.chebyshevMeasureT_univ (TauCeti/.../Chebyshev/Measure.lean:46) gives mass π. Normalization by π and affine transport supply the single-interval measure carrier, but the potential/capacity identification remains route 1.

items.name: Admissible weights, weighted equilibrium measures and modified Robin constants
items.statement: For compact Σ ⊂ ℂ, an admissible weight w is upper semicontinuous, nonnegative and positive on a set of positive logarithmic capacity. Set Q=−log w, I_w(ν)=I(ν)+2∫Q dν on probability measures. The unique weighted equilibrium measure µ_w minimizes I_w; write V_w=I_w(µ_w) and F_w=V_w−∫Q dµ_w. Smith uses the positive continuous weight w=e^{U^µ} on compact real Σ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.7 proof, pp.7–8; [24] Definition I.1.1 and Theorem I.1.3
items.note: Plan general compact complex carriers; the specialization in 58 identifies the particular minimizer. No unbounded-set admissibility convention is silently imposed.

items.name: Identification of the weighted equilibrium measure for w=e^{U^µ}
items.statement: If µ is a Hölder probability measure supported on compact Σ⊂ℝ and w=e^{U^µ}, the weighted equilibrium measure µ_w equals µ and F_w=0. Here Q=−U^µ, so U^µ+Q is identically zero on Σ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.7 proof p.8; [24] Theorem I.3.1
items.note: This is the exact weighted-equilibrium characterization used by Smith; it is distinct from mere existence/uniqueness of an unweighted equilibrium measure.

items.name: Existence of asymptotically extremal monic polynomials at every degree
items.statement: For the compact real Σ and weight w=e^{U^µ} of 58, there are real monic Q_n of degree n, all roots in Σ, with ‖w^nQ_n‖_Σ^{1/n}→e^{−F_w}=1.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.7 proof p.7; [24] Theorem III.1.9
items.note: Smith inserts these polynomials into the missing degrees before applying the zero-distribution theorem. The extracted specialization has the same real support hypotheses as his use.

items.name: Zero distribution of asymptotically extremal weighted polynomials
items.statement: In the setting of 58, if real monic P_n has degree n, all roots in Σ and ‖w^nP_n‖_Σ^{1/n}→e^{−F_w}, then its normalized zero measures converge weak* to µ_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.7 proof p.8; [24] Theorem III.4.2
items.note: Imported source of item 14 after filling missing degrees with 59. This extraction records the used real-support specialization, not an unrestricted complex zero-distribution assertion.

items.name: Principle of domination for logarithmic potentials
items.statement: Let µ,ν be finite positive measures with compact support in ℂ, ν(ℂ)≤µ(ℂ), and I(µ)<∞. If U^µ≤U^ν+c holds µ-almost everywhere, then it holds everywhere in ℂ.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), proof of Proposition 2.5 p.36; Lemma 5.10 p.38; Proposition 5.17 p.44; [24] Theorem II.3.2
items.note: Equal-mass comparisons suffice in Smith. The mass inequality direction and finite-energy hypothesis are confirmed by Saff, arXiv:1010.3760, Theorem 2.8 p.182 (PDF p.18). I.1.4 is Frostman, not this theorem.

items.name: Frostman bounds for the equilibrium potential
items.statement: For compact Σ⊂ℂ of positive capacity κ and equilibrium measure µ_Σ, U^{µ_Σ}(z)≤−log κ for every z∈ℂ, and equality holds quasi-everywhere on Σ (outside a capacity-zero set).
items.note: For an interval, continuity removes the exceptional set. Keep the global inequality and the quasi-everywhere equality separate; no unsupported everywhere equality on arbitrary compact sets.

items.name: Weak lower semicontinuity of logarithmic energy
items.statement: For probability measures µ_n supported on a fixed compact K⊂ℂ, weak* convergence µ_n→µ implies I(µ)≤liminf_n I(µ_n), with extended-real energy for kernel −log|z−w|.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Proposition 5.7 proof pp.35–36; [24] Theorem I.6.8
items.note: Truncate the kernel from above after a constant lower shift. This is the input transferring I≤0 from the smoothed and sweetened measures.

items.name: Countable sets are polar
items.statement: Every countable subset of ℂ has logarithmic capacity zero.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Proposition 2.5 proof p.36; potential-theory background [22,24]
items.note: The discarded set consists of one-point connected components, which is countable under Theorem 1.5, not necessarily the isolated points (E6).

items.name: Finite-energy measures give no mass to polar sets
items.statement: If µ is a finite positive compactly supported measure with I(µ)<∞, then µ(E)=0 for every Borel set E of logarithmic capacity zero.
items.note: With the kernel −log|z−w|, the required bound is above, I<∞ (E7); a lower bound alone is automatic on a compact support. Apply after 39 and 64.

items.name: Continuity of capacity under increasing Borel unions
items.statement: For increasing bounded Borel sets E_n⊂ℂ, cap(⋃E_n)=lim_n cap(E_n), using inner logarithmic capacity. Removing a polar subset does not change capacity.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), implicit choice of Σ₁ with capacity>1 in proof of Proposition 2.5 p.36; [22,24]
items.note: Enumerate the nondegenerate interval components of Σ and discard its countable polar one-point components. Their finite unions increase to a set of the same capacity, so some finite union already has capacity>1. This supplies the otherwise unstated step before sweetening.

items.name: Remez bound used when removing a polynomial root
items.statement: If a complex polynomial Q has degree at most m≥1 and E⊂[−1,1] is measurable with length at least 2−m^{−2}, then max_[−1,1]|Q|≤e^5 sup_E|Q|. After affine scaling this applies on each short interval I in Lemma 2.8, whose omitted part has relative length at most (2m²)^{−1}.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.8 p.8 and Corollary 3.3 p.13; [9] Erdélyi (1992), Theorem 1
items.note: Exact specialization stated and used on Smith p.8; do not identify ordinary interpolation with this sup-norm inequality. Route once with potential theory; no existing Remez owner found in the current roadmap/packet search.

items.name: Flatness bound for simplices and the polynomial adjustment application
items.statement: For an n-dimensional simplex S, n≤Flt(S)≤C n(1+log n), where Flt(S) is the supremum of lattice widths of lattice-free affine images of S and C is absolute. Lattice width is the infimum, over nonzero dual lattice vectors u, of sup_K⟨u,x⟩−inf_K⟨u,x⟩. The corresponding polynomial-size vertex/facet extension supplies the O(n log(2n)) translate-hits-lattice bound used for Smith’s real cofactor ℓ¹ body.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Theorem 3.2 proof p.13; [5] BLPS Corollary 2.5, author-copy PDF p.10, with Theorem 2.4 and discussion pp.2–3

items.name: Nonzero multivariate polynomials do not vanish on a sufficiently large grid
items.statement: For a finite set of variables over an integral domain, if degree_i F<|S_i| for each finite grid S_i and F vanishes on ∏S_i then F=0. For a nonzero polynomial of total degree d over ℂ, choose a degree-d nonzero monomial t and grids {0,…,t_i}; the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz gives a nonvanishing evaluation at nonnegative integers b_i with Σb_i≤d.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 2.10 proof p.9, substituting for the multivariate Gregory–Newton argument [25, (2),(3)]
items.note: Mathlib/Combinatorics/Nullstellensatz.lean:67 and :240 were read at the pin. Applying d≤2(n−deg G)−1 proves both the printed total bound and the weaker individual bounds. No Salzer prerequisite needs to be planned.

items.name: Separation of an open convex set from a disjoint convex set
items.statement: In a real topological vector space, disjoint convex sets s,t with s open admit a continuous linear functional f and u with f(a)<u≤f(b) for a∈s,b∈t. For nonempty sets this functional is nonzero, and negating it gives Smith’s orientation.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Theorem 5.11 p.39 and Proposition 5.17 p.44, citing Klee [16]
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/Separation.lean:95–97 supplies the statement; use the nonempty W interior and V in finite-dimensional ℝ^{N+1}. E5 is a separate root/zero-coefficient issue, not a gap in this library theorem.

items.name: Tietze extension of continuous real functions
items.statement: A continuous real function on a closed subset of a normal space extends continuously to the ambient space. In Lemma 5.4 extend f on compact Σ to [−C,C], then use uniform continuity there.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), Lemma 5.4 proof pp.33–34, citing Willard [37], Theorem 15.8
items.note: Mathlib/Topology/TietzeExtension.lean:68 and :77; the subtype inclusion of a closed set is a closed embedding, and ℝ is a Tietze-extension space.

items.name: Sylvester-determinant discriminant
items.statement: For a polynomial over a commutative ring, its discriminant is the signed determinant of the derivative Sylvester matrix. Together with the resultant specialization and coprimality API, it supplies the discriminant polynomial used in Lemma 2.10.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean:930. The specific degree estimate and specialization bookkeeping in Smith remain part of item 17; the generic discriminant is not missing. AUDIT-18 CA.3 marks it built.

items.name: Blichfeldt's theorem
items.statement: For a countable measurable additive group action with invariant measure and a fundamental domain F, if a null-measurable s has measure greater than that of F, then two distinct translates of s meet.
items.locator: arXiv:2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024), geometry-of-numbers background to §3, pp.12–16
items.note: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean:52–55; AUDIT-02 GN.1 built. Imported background, not the BLPS flatness supplier.

items.name: Minkowski's first convex-body theorem
items.statement: In a finite-dimensional real normed space with an additive Haar measure and a countable lattice with fundamental domain F, a convex symmetric set s with µ(F)·2^dim<µ(s) contains a nonzero lattice point.

prerequisites.why: Weighted admissibility/equilibrium/Robin constant (Definition I.1.1, Theorems I.1.3 and I.3.1); extremal polynomials and zero distribution (III.1.9, III.4.2); Frostman bounds (I.1.4, I.1.9); lower semicontinuity of energy (I.6.8); domination (II.3.2, NOT I.1.4); and the interval equilibrium measure (Example I.3.5). These are exact locators as cited by Smith pp.7–8,32,34,36,38,44. The accessible 13-page book file is front matter only, not a fresh full reading of these chapters. General balayage at Smith p.45 is future work; mass one in Lemma 5.2 can instead use u=1/t.

prerequisites.why: The source, cited as [22], for the definition of capacity as the supremum of e^{−I(µ)} and for the existence and uniqueness of the unweighted equilibrium measure of a compact set of positive capacity. Also countable polar sets, finite-energy measures annihilating polar sets, and continuity of inner capacity under increasing Borel unions in the reduction on p.36. prerequisites.citation: M. Fekete and G. Szegő, On algebraic equations with integral coefficients whose roots belong to a given point set, Math. Z. 63 (1955), 158–172

prerequisites.citation: Raphael M. Robinson, Conjugate algebraic integers in real point sets, Math. Z. 84 (1964), 415–427
prerequisites.why: The coefficient-adjustment technique of §4 and the proof that a real set of capacity greater than 1 contains infinitely many complete sets of conjugate algebraic integers; Proposition 4.1 follows Robinson's approach, and the capacity-1 case of Theorem 1.5 is known only in the special cases he treated.

prerequisites.citation: Christopher J. Smyth, The mean values of totally real algebraic integers, Math. Comp. 42 (1984), 663–681, and Totally positive algebraic integers of small trace, Ann. Inst. Fourier 34 (1984), 1–28
prerequisites.why: The auxiliary-polynomial method and the bound λ_SSS ≥ 1.7719 that the whole subject builds on; the counting measure µ_P is taken from the first of these papers. Smyth's later note An inequality for polynomials (1999) is where he suggests that 2 may not be the smallest limit point, the reading this paper vindicates.

The numbered equations (8), (10) and (11) of that appendix are used in Example 5.16.

routes.title: Logarithmic potential theory and the distribution of conjugates of algebraic integers
routes.brief: Plan logarithmic potential theory first for arbitrary compact subsets of ℂ: logarithmic potentials, energy, capacity, equilibrium measures, Frostman inequalities, domination, polar sets, lower semicontinuity and continuity of capacity. Include admissible external fields, weighted equilibrium measures and modified Robin constants with the precise weighted polynomial inputs of Lemma 2.7. Then specialize to real compact sets for Hölder measures, Remez root removal, Chebyshev equioscillation, pruned/complementary polynomials, Robinson–Fekete–Szegő coefficient adjustment, convolution and sweetening. Final targets are Smith Theorem 1.5 (real compact Σ with countably many components and capacity>1), Theorem 5.11 (Smyth optimality), Theorem 1.1 (λ_SSS<1.89831), and Propositions 5.12–5.13/Corollary 1.3 on extreme finite-field point counts. Import counting/finite measures, weak convergence and compactness, resultants, discriminants, grid nonvanishing, Tietze and separation directly from the pinned libraries; import only Minkowski II and the polynomial flatness/evaluation results from GN.1, and classical trace constants/auxiliary inequalities and Lemma 2.10 from CA.6/CA.3. Import general F_q Honda–Tate once from the shared AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli Part II family and Weil estimates from DWP.1/R34.2. Expose the general complex capacity/equilibrium interface to PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25/potential-generalization-2.5.27 in ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds, and to CA.6’s Dimitrov hedgehog-capacity consumer; their specialized holonomy, Dubinin and arithmetic-rationality results are not replanned here. The restrictions to real Σ and capacity>1 concern the arithmetic realization Theorem 1.5: this brief does not extend that theorem to complex Σ or capacity=1. Keep the common potential foundations upstream of CA.6’s Dimitrov consumer; the separate classical trace constant feeds only the later Smith arithmetic stages, avoiding a dependency cycle. Exact endpoints: for compact Σ⊂ℝ with countably many connected components and cap(Σ)>1, a probability µ is a weak* limit of root measures of distinct irreducible monic integer polynomials supported on Σ iff ∫log|Q|dµ≥0 for every nonzero Q∈ℤ[X] (1.5). For closed Σ with the same component/capacity hypotheses and continuous F satisfying F(x)/log|x|→+∞ at infinity when Σ is unbounded, the liminf mean F on conjugates equals the supremum of λ for which F≥λ+Σa_i log|Q_i| with positive a_i and nonzero integer Q_i (5.11). For all sufficiently large square prime powers q there are infinitely many F_q-simple A with #A(F_q)≥(q+2√q−0.89831)^{dim A} and infinitely many with #A(F_q)≤(q−2√q+2.89831)^{dim A} (1.3); Proposition 5.12 gives the two limiting normalized extremes exp(λ(Σ,F)) and exp(−λ(Σ,−F)) for Σ=[−2√q,2√q], F(x)=log|q+1−x|.
routes.reason: There is no existing general logarithmic-potential owner in the current atlas/roadmap definitions. The accepted Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang route and CA.6 packet already need compact complex capacity and equilibrium measures, so real-only foundations would be too narrow. The new roadmap owns those common foundations and Smith’s applications; source/Part II routes below own shared arithmetic and convex inputs. The review’s former negative Honda–Tate search is superseded by the accepted Lipnowski–Tsimerman extraction.

GN.1 owns lattice convex geometry and already plans both sides of Minkowski II. Add Smith’s evaluation-polytope/Vandermonde specialization (23), polynomial coefficient adjustment (21), and its independent BLPS flatness supplier (68). Import built Blichfeldt/Minkowski I and GN.0 carriers; never replan them. The current GN packet has no BLPS flatness node, so this source contribution is distinct from item 52’s existing planned theorem.

CA.6 plans special algebraic numbers and the Mahler measure — the house, the Pisot and Salem classes, selected lower bounds and finiteness statements through exact conjugate data — which is MSC 11R06, the same classification as the trace problem. The classical material routed there is the notion of a totally positive algebraic integer with its trace ratio, the constant λ_SSS with the chain of bounds from Schur's e^{1/2} ≤ λ_SSS ≤ 2 through Siegel, Smyth and the current 1.793145 ≤ λ_SSS ≤ 2, the statement of the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem in Borwein's form, and Smyth's auxiliary-polynomial method with the resultant argument that makes it work. These are classical statements about special algebraic numbers that the layer should own and that the new roadmap should import; the paper's own theorems about them are not routed here. Separately, CA.3 plans integer-polynomial arithmetic — integer-valued polynomials, irreducibility, resultants and discriminants — and is the owner of Lemma 2.10, that a small nonnegative integral combination of integer polynomials, divided by their gcd, is squarefree of the expected degree. That is a statement about polynomial arithmetic with no potential theory in it.

routes.brief: Combine this request with PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/honda-tate and /tate-hom in the parent’s single Part II design. Develop the classification of simple abelian varieties over arbitrary finite fields F_q by conjugacy classes of Weil q-numbers, including Tate’s rational Hom theorem and the multiplicities/endomorphism data needed to recover Frobenius polynomials and normalized point counts. Import abelian varieties, Tate modules and realizations from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli and the Weil estimates from DWP.1/R34.2. Preserve the general prime-power field here even when later counting applications specialize to prime fields. Export the classification to Smith’s LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers route; Smith’s optimization Propositions 5.12–5.13 and Corollary 1.3 are consumers in that route, not duplicate foundational targets here. Faltings’s number-field isogeny theorem is not the supplier of Honda–Tate. The core correspondence is a bijection between F_q-isogeny classes of simple abelian varieties and conjugacy classes of q-Weil algebraic integers π; for ℓ≠char(F_q), Hom_Fq(A,B)⊗ℚ_ℓ≅Hom_Gal(V_ℓA,V_ℓB). Include the relation P_A=m_π^e and 2 dim A=e·deg(m_π), rather than silently dropping the Honda–Tate multiplicity.

At such roots, the proof claims the inequality because its left side is finite while its right side is −∞.
sourceIssues.correction: Discard the Q_i with a_i = 0, so that the remaining coefficients are positive as the definition requires. At points x ∈ Σ that are roots only of discarded Q_i, the right side is then finite, and the inequality needs an argument. If x is a limit point of Σ, use continuity. If x is an isolated point of Σ, perturb, for example by giving the relevant Q_i a small positive coefficient at a small cost in λ. On compact parts the cost is at most η times an upper bound for log|Q_i|; outside a sufficiently large compact set, growth condition (5.11) absorbs the finitely many added logarithmic terms. Let the resulting loss in λ tend to zero.
sourceIssues.reason: When a_i = 0 the term a_i log|Q_i(x)| is 0 · (−∞), not −∞. At a root x of such a Q_i that is not a root of any Q_j with a_j > 0, the right side is finite. The Dirac measure δ_x is not in M_N, since ∫ log|Q_i| dδ_x = −∞, so the separation inequality does not cover x, and the printed justification ("the right is −∞") fails. The definition of λ_Smyth also demands positive coefficients, which the separation argument does not supply. The conclusion λ(Σ, F) = λ_Smyth(Σ, F) is expected to survive the repair. Noted by the extraction (item 114), which left the perturbation as an outstanding step. sourceIssues.printed: The source expresses Σ as its isolated points together with ∪_{k≥1} Σ_k, where every Σ_k is compact and a finite union of intervals, with Σ_k ⊆ Σ_{k+1} for every k ≥ 1.
sourceIssues.correction: "… as the union of its set of one-point components with a set of the form ∪_{k≥1} Σ_k …". The one-point components form a countable set, which is all the next sentence uses.
sourceIssues.reason: A one-point component need not be isolated. Σ = {0} ∪ ⋃_{n≥1}[1/(2n+1), 1/(2n)] ∪ [1, 6] is compact, has countably many components and capacity greater than 1 (it contains [1, 6], of capacity 5/4). Its component {0} is not isolated, and 0 lies in no compact finite union of intervals inside Σ, because every neighbourhood of 0 meets gaps of Σ. So the printed decomposition fails. With one-point components in place of isolated points the decomposition holds (the other components are countably many closed intervals, and Σ_k is the union of the first k of them), and the argument that μ gives this countable set measure 0 is unchanged. sourceIssues.correction: Its roots lie in the convex hull [min Σ,max Σ]; its degree is 3k₀. Hence on Σ its absolute value is at most diam(Σ)^{3k₀}, the constant needed for the lower bound.

A pruned polynomial has roots only in Σ, so this root remains in the quotient. The corrected convex-hull bound follows from alternation and leaves the lemma intact. sourceIssues.printed: The source states the minimal-shift claim for 0≤k≤N/a, including k=0.
sourceIssues.correction: Write Q=B+N with B=Q₀+Σ ε_iT_i. For every shift N′∈[0,N), minimality gives a root α with |B(α)+N′|<a/2. Each root contributes an open interval of real shifts of length at most a. At most n such intervals cover [0,N), hence N≤na, proving (4.9).
sourceIssues.reason: At k=0 the printed assertion contradicts the defining lower bound |Q(α)|≥a/2 for every root. The interval-cover argument works for real or nonreal roots (intersection of a radius-a/2 disk with a horizontal line has length at most a), and establishes the exact required bound. If n=0 there are no roots and the minimal shift is N=0; the division by n is used only for n>0. Verified against Definition 4.6 and the page image.
